Al Azm Palace · Damascus

قصر العظم · درة العمارة الدمشقية

Built in 1749 CE by As'ad Pasha al-Azm, governor of Damascus during the Ottoman era, Al Azm Palace is considered one of the finest surviving exemplars of 18th-century Damascene domestic architecture.

Ablaq Masonry (الأبلق): The distinctive alternating courses of local black volcanic basalt from Hauran and cream-colored limestone from the Syrian hills create monumental rhythmic facades.
The Great Iwan (الإيوان الكبير): A grand monumental vaulted hall facing north toward the central courtyards, designed to catch cooling summer breezes and host dignified guests on its raised marble dais.
Courtyard Water Gardens: Multi-tiered octagonal fountains and reflection pools are surrounded by fragrant bitter orange trees (naranj), night-blooming jasmine, and bougainvillea.

This 3D model brings the palace's architectural nuances to life directly in your web browser, allowing open exploration without requiring Blender or 3D software.
